title: Zoom in: which tier answers a dashboard query
caption: Read the coarsest tier the range allows, fill the part that tier doesn't cover yet from a finer one, and label what is still provisional.

steps.text: An artist asks for daily plays over the last 90 days.
Too long for minutes or hours: read day rows, one per day per track.
Today has no day row yet, so the tier doesn't cover the whole range.
Fill today from its hour rows, and the current hour from minute rows.
Mark days that recon has not finalised as provisional, then return the series.

scenarios.name: Last-hour panel
scenarios.summary: A live panel of the last hour reads minute rows directly: about 60 per track, nothing to fill.

steps.text: Read minute rows. They are written as windows close, so they are already as fresh as the stream.
Everything is provisional for now; the label says so.

scenarios.name: Hour rollup behind
scenarios.summary: The job that rolls minutes into hours is three hours behind. The router fills the gap from minute rows instead of showing a dip.

steps.text: A 7-day chart reads hour rows, but the last three hours are missing.
Fill those hours by summing minute rows: a few hundred extra rows, still fast.
The chart is correct, with a "data as of" note; an alert on rollup lag is already firing.

scenarios.name: Monthly statement
scenarios.summary: The royalty statement for a closed month reads day rows too, but it accepts only final ones.

steps.text: A one-month range goes to day rows.
The month is closed, so every day has a row: nothing to fill.
Unlike a dashboard, the statement refuses provisional days: if recon has not finished a day, the statement waits for it.
